title: The Temple’s notice to the nations
subtitle: The Temple Warning Inscription

images.caption: A fragment of one of the warning stones, in the Israel Museum, Jerusalem.

p: A stone notice from Herod’s Temple, written in Greek for visitors from the nations. Anyone could come into the great outer court, and people from many nations came to pray there. Notices like this one stood at the low barrier around the inner courts. They told foreigners that whoever went further would be responsible for his own death.

Holiness in the Temple was marked in steps, and everyone had limits. Women went as far as their own court, Israelite men as far as the court of Israel, only priests served at the altar, and only the high priest entered the Holy of Holies, once a year on Yom Kippur. Josephus describes these notices in Greek and Latin. Acts 21:28–29 tells how Shaul (Paul) was falsely accused of bringing Trophimus the Ephesian past them.
facts: A complete stone in 1871 (Charles Clermont-Ganneau); this fragment in 1935, near the Lions’ Gate
Herod’s Temple, late 1st century BC to AD 70
Complete stone: Istanbul Archaeology Museums; fragment: the Israel Museum, Jerusalem
